proof_summary: A period \(T\) is characterized by \(n\mid T^p\) and \(n\mid pT\): necessity follows by testing shifts at \(0\) and \(1\), factoring the latter binomial difference and canceling a factor coprime to \(T\), while sufficiency follows from divisibility of the intermediate binomial coefficients by the prime \(p\). Prime-factor divisibility then shows every period is a multiple of \(n/p\) when \(p^2\mid n\), and a multiple of \(n\) otherwise, with those respective bounds themselves satisfying the two conditions.
